Title: Genital tuberculosis in females
Abstract: The two imaging techniques useful in the diagnosis of @DISEASE_Tuberculosis_Female_Genital @DISEASE_MESH:D014384 @@@FGTB@@@ are <m>hysterosalpingography</m> (HSG) and ultrasonography (USG). HSG evaluates the internal structure of the <m>female</m> <m>genital</m> <m>tract</m> and <m>tubal</m> patency whereas USG allows simultaneous evaluation of ovarian, uterine and extrapelvic <m>involvement</m>.

Title: Hysterosalpingographic findings in women with genital tuberculosis
Abstract: HSG is a helpful imaging modality for evaluating the internal architecture of the <m>female</m> <m>genital</m> <m>tract</m> and is the most invaluable procedure in the assessment of @DISEASE_Fallopian_Tube_Diseases @DISEASE_MESH:D005184 @@@<m>tubal</m> factor <m>infertility</m>@@@ in developing countries.
